sources.entry: Fullstack Dev Skills by jeffallan - A comprehensive Claude Code plugin with 65 specialized skills covering full-stack development across a wide range of specific frameworks. Features 9 project workflow commands for Jira/Confluence integration and, notably, an interesting approach to context engineering via a /common-ground command that surfaces Claude's hidden assumptions about your project. summary.one_liner: A Claude Code plugin bundling 67 specialized skills for full-stack development, plus context-engineering and Jira/Confluence project workflow commands.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a plugin of 67 specialized skills across 12 categories, covering languages, backend and frontend frameworks, infrastructure, APIs, testing, DevOps, security, data/ML, and platform specialists. Skills activate automatically based on the request, for example a NestJS authentication request activates a NestJS expert skill that loads a specific reference file. Multi-skill workflows chain skills together for feature development, bug investigation, and security hardening. A /common-ground command is described as surfacing Claude's hidden assumptions about a project. Nine project workflow commands manage epics from discovery through retrospectives, integrating with Jira and Confluence via an Atlassian MCP server. The README points to external guides for the full skill list, installation methods, and command reference, so the specifics of individual skills are not in this README.
use_cases: Full-stack feature development with specialized framework guidance
Surfacing hidden assumptions in a project with /common-ground
Managing epics and sprints through Jira and Confluence
Debugging workflows combining framework and test skills
Reference lookup for specific frameworks like NestJS or React
stack: Atlassian MCP server (for Jira/Confluence workflow commands)
notable: 67 framework and domain skills that activate automatically from the request
/common-ground command for surfacing Claude's assumptions about a project
Nine workflow commands covering epics from discovery through retrospectives
Multi-skill workflow chains such as Feature Development and Security Hardening
About 371 reference files for deep-dive material
caveats: Workflow commands require a separately configured Atlassian MCP server
Full skill list, command reference, and installation details live in external documentation rather than the README
